newsitem.title: UK: British ex-minister loses deselection battle.
newsitem.headline: British ex-minister loses deselection battle.

text.p: Former Conservative government minister Sir Nicholas Scott on Monday lost his battle to avoid being deselected for one of the ruling party's safest parliamentary seats.
A secret ballot of almost 1,000 members in his affluent London constituency voted "by a very considerable margin" to choose another candidate for the next general, due by next May.
"There was a certain sadness but he bore it like a man," constituency chairman Andrew Dalton said after the vote.
Scott was found face down in the road by police after a reception at a Conservative Party conference in October. He denied he was drunk, blaming his condition on painkillers.
In a rearguard action to save his political career, Scott said in a series of interviews that he had decided to become "absolutely teetotal."
Prime Minister John Major has a majority of just one in the 651-seat House of Commons. But Scott will not step down before the election.
Scott was minister of state for Northern Ireland from 1986 to 1987 and minister of state for social security and the disabled from 1987 to 1994.
